profile: XNA 4.0 full runtime superset projected to Java 17, plus the CNA extension surface

glContexts.OPENGL33: OpenGL 4.6 core on AMD Radeon 780M, 4.5 core on llvmpipe under Xvfb

qualifiedRuntime.note: A multi-renderer CNA build: five renderers compiled in and one chosen before the first GraphicsDevice through the CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERER environment variable, or through GraphicsRenderer.setPreferred -- which is the safe way, because the environment variable naming a renderer this build lacks aborts the process at library load (JAVA-UPSTREAM-017). The whole suite runs green on each of the five. The platform is SDL3 rather than HEADLESS because a GPU renderer needs a native window; the suite can be pointed at a virtual display, and was. cnaHead is the commit the qualified library was built from; the commit is not what pins this, cnaInventorySha256 is -- later dependency commits that leave the C API headers alone leave that hash unchanged and these measurements standing, and one that moves the headers changes it and does not.

capabilities.detail: The ownership graph and canonical XACT routes are verified; no licensed authored bank corpus qualified successful authored playback.
NULL-audio no-device behavior and native routes are verified; real capture hardware and BufferReady timing are not qualified.
Java safely exposes a PARENT_OWNED transient alias; CNA ABI 0.7 lacks XNA two-buffer identity and a frame generation token.
Metadata and player control routes execute, but HEADLESS produced no decoded frame and no qualified video asset established successful decode.
Canonical empty/default platform collections execute; populated catalog, token, thumbnail, and picture-store behavior require a real supported platform.
Java enforces XNA canonical containment before JNI; qualified CNA ABI 0.7 itself accepts parent traversal and cannot yet be credited with the guarantee.
Registration, queueing, owner-thread dispatch, containment, shutdown discard, and injected delivery are verified; no real OS device transition was observed.

The selected component lifecycle uses three canonical ABI 0.7 routes. Real sign-in/Guide/network/title-update services are absent, and current CNA HEAD cannot build the C API in either networking configuration.
Value conversion, ordered decomposition, reconstruction, and culture are implemented; Java has no CLR ComponentModel designer host, context, descriptor services, or attribute filtering.

capabilities.surface: Gamer, SignedInGamer, SignedInGamerCollection, Guide, GamerProfile, GamerPrivileges, GameDefaults, GamerPresence
capabilities.detail: Every member reaches a real CNA route and CNA answers: it publishes a local signed-in roster on this runtime and implements the Guide in process. No Xbox Live service is present, so what a real sign-in, a real friends list or a real achievement award would report is not qualified. Guide.IsScreenSaverEnabled does not round-trip, because CNA accepts the request and the headless platform does not honour it.

Every event now has a native producer. The JNI callbacks record each event and Java drains the record right after pumping the dispatcher or the session, so an event arrives on the game thread during Update, as XNA raises it. GameStarted and GameEnded are verified end to end on a local session. The rest share that producer and that drain, but a real GamerJoined, HostChanged or SignedIn needs a second machine or a live sign-in, neither of which took part in this qualification.

The whole family reaches CNA's avatar routes. XNA's avatars are an Xbox 360 facility; what a real avatar description, a real animation clip or a rendered avatar looks like is not qualified on this platform.

capabilities.surface: NetworkSession, AvailableNetworkSession, NetworkGamer, LocalNetworkGamer, NetworkMachine, NetworkSessionProperties
capabilities.detail: Creation, discovery, rosters, state and properties reach CNA. Only a SystemLink search reaches real discovery in CNA, and no second machine took part in this qualification, so a real joined session is not qualified.

Managed by design: XNA's are a BinaryReader and BinaryWriter over a memory stream, so Position and Length keep exactly that meaning over one cursor. Every value type round-trips in XNA's own layout, verified in the managed tests.

Availability, the render pipeline settings, the physically based material and the ASCII post-process effect reach CNA. This build carries the extended layer, so availability reports true; a build without it answers false and the routes raise ExtensionNotSupportedException rather than downgrading. The CRT and depth-reduction effects are not bound yet: backlog JAVA-EXT-004.

The platform, desktop operating system, renderer name, backend category and maturity, application title and CNA's logger all reach CNA and are asserted against what this build reports: Desktop, Linux, HEADLESS, Diagnostic, Supported.

Accelerometer, Gyroscope, Compass and Motion create, report state, round-trip their sampling interval and release their owned handle against the live runtime. This host has none of the four: every one reports NotSupported, getIsDataValid is false, and a reading is refused with IllegalStateException rather than answered with zeros, which is CNA's own contract and what the tests assert. A reading from real hardware is not qualified here.

Mice, keyboards, touch devices and host motion sensors enumerate as immutable snapshots with the host's own identifier and name; zero devices is an ordinary answer on this headless host. Hot plug is verified end to end without hardware, because CNA exposes the same event its platform layer raises: a raised connection reaches a Java listener on the game thread during FrameworkDispatcher.Update, in raise order, and stops when the listener or the native subscription is released. The registrations are process-wide and were proved to survive one game being destroyed and another created. Real hardware being plugged in was not exercised.

Enumeration, capabilities and snapshot capture reach CNA and hot plug is verified end to end through CNA's own raise routes. This host has no joystick, so the branch that was exercised is the documented one: an identifier nothing is connected to captures successfully with every list empty rather than failing or reporting a device of zeros. A snapshot copies all four arrays and releases the native handle before returning, so it carries no lifetime; capturing consumes trackball motion, which is CNA's contract. No real axis, button, hat or trackball value was read here.

Enumeration, opening from a device id, a joystick or the mouse, capabilities, rumble, gain, autocentre, pause and resume, and the six typed effect families all reach CNA. This host has no force feedback, so what was exercised is CNA's documented closed-device contract: opening succeeds, the device reports itself closed, its maxima are absent rather than zero, and every operation is a safe no-op reporting that nothing was applied. The effect encoding is verified independently of hardware, field by field, because a value landing in the wrong slot would be silent. No motor was actually driven.

The game-pad identity, battery, light bar, trigger motors, touchpad fingers, button labels and on-pad sensors; the keyboard's layout-dependent and layout-independent key naming, scancode translation and modifier state; the mouse's capture, relative mode, desktop position, warp and click event; and mouse-driven touch emulation. The mouse-touch emulation flag and the mouse click event round-trip against the live runtime. No game pad is connected here, so the pad readings report absent rather than zero and were not read from hardware; the keyboard name round trip is asserted only when the headless host names the key at all.

Composition drafts and candidate lists reach a Java listener through a second event transport that copies each borrowed UTF-8 view inside CNA's callback and frees the copy before Java sees it. Verified end to end against the live runtime with accented Latin, CJK and a supplementary code point; with byte offsets mapped to Java string indices, including offsets that land inside a character and are reported as naming nothing; with an empty composition and an empty candidate list delivered as real events; and with 400 raised events over a 64-deep queue, where every one is either delivered intact or counted as dropped. Ordering across the numeric and string transports is proved by a sequence merge, and the assertion fails if the merge is removed. No input method is installed on this host, so the events were raised through CNA's own dispatch rather than by a person typing.

CnaModel.From(Model) builds CNA's own model over the buffers and effects an XNA model already owns, retained rather than copied, and CNA then draws it in one call and computes its bone transforms. Verified against an authored XNA 4.0 .xnb cube from the sibling CNA checkout: the graph round-trips bone for bone, mesh for mesh and part for part, CNA reports the same BasicEffect identity the managed reader built, its absolute bone transforms match the managed arithmetic exactly, written bone transforms read back, and the native draw is accepted on the headless renderer. Loading through CNA's own content manager is not offered: cna_content_manager_load_model produces a model that segfaults during teardown for any asset with a mesh part, recorded with a C reproduction as JAVA-UPSTREAM-004. The cameras, skins and material variants CnaModel reports are therefore always empty here, because only a CNA-imported model carries them.

CNA's own compiled content format, beside XNB rather than instead of it. Verified end to end against the live runtime: a texture built from four distinct pixels is encoded by CNA's own encoder, parsed back from memory and from a file, its metadata content name and asset type read back as written, every uncompressed chunk's CRC-32C recomputed and matched against the table of contents, and the decoded pixels compared byte for byte with the ones that went in and again after upload as an XNA Texture2D. A file written by CnbWriter with a game's own custom asset type and a mandatory chunk reads back with the same type, the same schema version, the same metadata and the same chunk bytes. The checked reader refuses a read past the end without moving its cursor and refuses an element count the remaining bytes cannot hold. CRC-32C is CNA's, not java.util.zip's CRC-32, and the hardware and portable paths are asserted to agree.

XNA's Guide draws its own on-screen keyboard and message box because an Xbox has a system overlay; CNA has none, so the request becomes the game's to show and that question has no XNA member. Verified end to end against the live runtime: Guide.BeginShowKeyboardInput makes a request the game finds pending with exactly the title, description and current text it asked for; discarding drops it unanswered; cancelling answers it and it stops being pending. Guide.BeginShowMessageBox reports the focused button the game does not otherwise know, and a click answers it. CNA's own plain renderer is reachable through Draw over a SpriteBatch, SpriteFont and white pixel the game supplies; drawing was not exercised on the headless renderer.

CNA reads ordinary source assets into compiled descriptions with no graphics or audio device: a PNG or JPEG becomes single-level RGBA8 texture data, optionally with one painted colour keyed to transparent, and a WAV becomes a PCM16 sound whose data chunk comes back byte for byte. Both are qualified against fixtures this repository authors -- a PNG written by the JDK and a WAV written from its published layout -- because the source formats are what is under test and a CNA-authored input would prove nothing.
capabilities.limitation: DDS cube import takes DXT1, DXT3 and DXT5 only. An uncompressed cube map is a real file this build declines, answering NOT_SUPPORTED with its own identity rather than failing as though the bytes were malformed; the first fixture written here was B8G8R8A8 and is what found that out.

capabilities.detail: The whole compiled-model graph reads and writes with no graphics device: bones, parts with their vertex and index bytes, meshes, the skinning skeleton with all three matrix sets, baked lights, and the glTF material factors with their eight texture names and seven per-slot states. Probed in C before binding, because JAVA-UPSTREAM-004 found CNA's content-manager model loader segfaulting during teardown; the .cnb path survives a build-encode-decode-destroy cycle cleanly.
capabilities.limitation: There is no CnbModelData.toModel(GraphicsDevice). XNA's Model has no public constructor and CNA offers no route that builds one from this description, so this is the tooling side of the file and a game still loads a model through the content manager. Animations are readable but not writable: cna_cnb_model_add_animation takes a nested descriptor graph the JNI generator refuses rather than guesses at, which is the same shape that blocks JAVA-EXT-007.

capabilities.detail: A compute program runs on the GPU and its output is compared against the same arithmetic done in Java: four integers doubled and offset by a uniform, read back through a storage buffer, exact. Verified on OPENGLES3 and OPENGL33; on HEADLESS, SOFTWARE and OPENGL4 every constructor in the family refuses and that refusal is what is asserted instead. Image binding is a separate question from having compute and the two really do come apart -- ES 3.1 says no, desktop 4.6 core says yes -- so it is asked rather than assumed. The dialect is GLSL ES: every compute program inside CNA own engine layer opens with #version 310 es, which both capable renderers accept, while desktop GLSL compiles only on the one whose context really is desktop GL. UPSTREAM_CNA_BLOCKED is JAVA-UPSTREAM-012: a source that does not compile is reported as an internal failure rather than as a shader carrying a compile error, which makes two documented routes unreachable for the case they exist for.

The meter reduces a frame to one number on the GPU, and the numbers are checked rather than the calls. A uniform grey of 8/255 measures 0.031373 and one of 240/255 measures 0.941176, both to within a thousandth; adaptation moves the exposure down for the brighter scene and up for the darker one; doubling the key value asks for more exposure from the same scene. Both capable renderers produce the same numbers. Needs compute, so on the other three renderers the constructor refuses and that is what is asserted.

The three bake routes take a callback CNA runs once per cube face, and on a renderer that can read a capture back it really runs: six faces for one probe and forty-eight for a two-by-two-by-two volume, each with the camera the baker chose for that face. The trampoline takes no global references -- the callback lives only inside the call -- and an exception it throws skips the remaining faces rather than being invoked with one pending, which is undefined in JNI. On HEADLESS the readback is refused, all three routes answer INVALID_STATE and the callback is entered zero times, which is asserted rather than skipped.

Registered once and run inside every later frame, so unlike the bake callbacks these are pinned by an explicit native token the pipeline owns and releases. The shadow callback runs first, inside begin; the transparent one second, inside end; once each per frame; and a failing callback result reaches the caller of the call that ran it. They run on every renderer, including HEADLESS -- what gates them is the settings, not the renderer, which corrects an earlier reading that had them blocked on hardware.

capabilities.surface: ShadowMap.getCasterEffect and its four siblings, DepthNormalPrepass, ClusteredForwardEffect, WeightedBlendedTransparency, RenderPipeline.getSceneTarget, PbrMaterialExtensions.hasClearcoatTexture and its eight siblings
capabilities.detail: Twenty-one routes lend a handle belonging to something else, on two opposite contracts that one word covered. A counted borrow blocks its lender destruction until it is given back; a retaining one keeps its lender alive and may outlive it. Each was measured in C before a facade was written, and nothing dangles: every lender that permits its own destruction really is retained by what it lent, and the one non-owning view answers INVALID_HANDLE afterwards rather than dereferencing freed memory. UPSTREAM_CNA_BLOCKED is JAVA-UPSTREAM-013, the one shadow map of four that does not count.

The two values this projection could previously only pin by layout. Both cross into CNA and never come back, and a renderer that draws nothing accepts either without doing anything observable -- a planted swap of the sampler address modes passed every test. On a renderer that draws, a filter is a pixel: a two-by-two checkerboard magnified sixteen times over is hard blocks under point filtering and a gradient under linear, and the same planted swap now fails. The context is verified in three fields rather than all of them: a blit output is decided by its source and destination handles, and film grain is seeded from the elapsed time, so swapping or zeroing those fails -- while swapping the normals and velocity slots still passes, because nothing reachable here reads them. Those leaves stay pinned by the layout gate alone, and that limit is recorded rather than glossed.

Which renderers this build has, and which one to try first -- asked of the library rather than read out of CMakeCache.txt, which is what this qualification had been doing while the routes sat unbound. Eighteen of the family's twenty-two routes are projected: the inventory, per-identity availability, per-identity category and maturity for any identity CNA defines whether or not this build has it, case-insensitive name parsing that treats an unknown name as an answer rather than a failure, the preference setters, the fallback chain with its history and CNA's own messages and reason names, the renderer actually running, and the test-only reset. Every setter is refused once a renderer exists and refused for a renderer this build lacks, both measured. UPSTREAM_CNA_BLOCKED is two findings: JAVA-UPSTREAM-018, three query routes that a GraphicsDevice resets and three named "current" that describe the compile-time default, none of them projected; and JAVA-UPSTREAM-017, the reason this exists -- CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERER naming a renderer this build lacks aborts the process while the library loads, before any Java frame exists, so no guard is possible and reading the inventory beforehand is the only defence.

A volume grading table is a cubical Texture3D with an edge between two and sixty-four, measured rather than read: CNA's declaration says "a cube", which reads both ways, and a TextureCube is refused with INVALID_HANDLE while a Texture3D of the same edge is accepted. The Java signature took a TextureCube and so could never have worked; nothing had caught it because no test had ever bound a volume table. Qualified on both sides of GraphicsCapability.Texture3D, because HEADLESS has no real 3D texture storage and refuses to allocate one -- where the storage exists the slot is exercised and read back, and where it does not the refusal is the one CNA documents.
